core.purpose: One coherent structural language and explicit trusted native composition.

architecture.purpose: Separate narrow source/semantic/IR/emission/runtime boundaries, reviewed arguments and actual recursive evidence.

identity.purpose: Complete versioned framed identities, exact collision rejection and original diagnostic source mappings.

assembly.purpose: One dependency-correct resolved C assembly with direct label transfers and enforced native-entry disappearance.

dependencies.purpose: One exact typed closure, distinct graph relations and no implicit instance/cache aliasing.

storage.purpose: Explicit per-context/instance/lexical storage and conservative general fallback without unclaimed identity/storage elimination.

pool.purpose: Stable block slots, generation retirement, intrusive reuse and nonreviving middle-block reclamation.

context.purpose: Isolated mutable runtime ownership and origin-first synchronized context/host admission.

invocation.purpose: Separate input preparation, target/result acquisition, explicit return links and scoped refusal/cleanup.

host.purpose: Explicit startup, entry/resume eligibility, completed/yielded/failed outcomes and nonexecuting disposal.

harness.purpose: Explicit C/assert leaves, recursive Make dependency order and preserved failed artifacts.

documentation.purpose: Exact canonical source/rendered destinations and complete meaningful file/case/header registration.

paths.purpose: Exact root-family-qualified Unicode/module topology and duplicate/alias detection without fallback.

layout.purpose: Byte-exact regions, compact punctuation, complete names and structural comment/marker nesting.

sections.purpose: Genuine zero-indent activation, canonical section order and constants-only/draft boundaries.

declarations.purpose: Exact nominal storage typing, ordered unconditional construction and separately retained interfaces.

lexical-inference.purpose: Source-ordered receiver classification and lexical foreach binding are resolved before ordinary executable uses.

literals.purpose: Raw bounded UTF-8 bytes acquire meaning only through the exact destination native constructor.

constants.purpose: Declaration-level dependency planning builds immutable context-local shared storage before root creation and excludes it from executable instances.

copy-boundary.purpose: Operation-scoped exact identity maps clone complete owned boundaries while preserving external handles and independent native value lifecycles.

copy-admission.purpose: Selection precedes exact identity/overlap and full ownership-tree availability checks; successful preflight protects all affected storage through hooks and destruction.

references.purpose: Nonowning context-local checked identities are formed independently from target acquisition and never revive after retirement or reclamation.

call-bindings.purpose: Whole-operation static validation precedes exact target admission, text-order input selection and declaration-order interface installation.

result-trees.purpose: Depth-first selected operations execute real retained result identities under bounded caller-owned protection frames and exact caller lexical lookup.

structured-control.purpose: Parsed lexical roots determine condition evaluation, loop backedges, release points and saved body positions without dynamic caller heuristics.

continuation-state.purpose: Saved labels and explicit generated control cells preserve only the suspended instance state, independently of any old caller or native C activation.

list-representation.purpose: Compact order indices and per-list checked membership records separate positional order, occurrence identity and stable target storage.

list-methods.purpose: Six intrinsic typed interfaces stage inputs and ephemeral results under exact service-token authority, then publish mutation or documented preflight refusal.

live-traversal.purpose: Fixed lexical cursor scans apply exact live-boundary corrections; membership origins guard removed occurrences independently from external target liveness.

native-contract.purpose: Generated standalone typed authoring headers and exact module-qualified protocol declarations agree with final assembly and supported target configuration.

native-values.purpose: Explicit native hooks obey fresh-storage, read-only conversion and independent immutable-backed value contracts; capability is an exact greatest fixed point over owned types.

lifecycle.purpose: Construction-state prefixes and publication-ordered roots govern exactly-once cleanup, preserving the primary failure across destructive commit and context disposal.

component-host.purpose: Explicit checked exports generate independent public headers, context/instance lifecycles and owned transports under one nonreentrant executor.

component-composition.purpose: Checked component names, public transports and explicit code pins isolate separately built libraries and retained child hosts without private dispatcher calls.

event-lifetime.purpose: Native-only completion tokens, retained event records and explicit callback ownership preserve wakeups without entering Ama or reviving retired submissions.

cooperative-tasks.purpose: Visible nominal task records and unique FIFO ready memberships reconcile explicit step phases, fresh enrollment identities, cancellation and finite round budgets.

parallel-messages.purpose: Context-private execution and synchronized native-owned bounded channels exchange checked independently reconstructed values with explicit close/abort/backpressure lifetimes.

failure-diagnostics.purpose: One owned application failure value remains separate from explicit immutable technical statuses and per-caller refusal snapshots; active source paths are streamed before cleanup.

relocation.purpose: Resolved whole-scope simultaneous identity mapping and exact original-span edits precede recoverable filesystem publication with repeatable interruption recovery.

evidence-checker.purpose: Exact canonical bijections, reviewed input provenance and actual compiled C case signatures prevent stale or invented conformance closure.

product-inputs.purpose: Exact immutable dependency/configuration snapshots and owned output publication retain deterministic products and invalidate changed consumers without overwriting authored inputs.

ARCH-01.argument: Cohesive production/test responsibility trees and the complete per-file registry preserve actual component ownership.

ARCH-02.argument: Parent orchestration delegates validation, preparation, commit and cleanup to documented narrow child operations.

ARCH-03.argument: Standalone headers and real component leaves verify narrow contracts, explicit lifetimes and ordinary separately compiled source units.

ARCH-04.argument: Independent and actual generated-parent cases accompany extracted meaningful boundaries; directory count alone is not evidence.

ARCH-05.argument: Exact identities, finite graph algorithms, checked resource policies and transition invariants are documented at their implementation boundaries.

ARCH-06.argument: Reviewed component arguments cover domains, laws, failure and complexity; source and rendered canonical links are checked.

ASYNC-01.argument: Yield returns only the immediate invocation and does not enroll tasks or schedule work; explicit task phases and the ordinary entry/resume distinction preserve this boundary.

ASYNC-02.argument: One context executor dispatches finite cooperative steps; explicit budgets limit completed steps, not preempt native execution. Yielded event waits retain no busy acquisition and runtime nested waiting remains distinct.

ASYNC-03.argument: Ordinary typed phase values distinguish Ready/Awaiting/Completed and agree with actual yield/completion; terminal application failure data are consumed only after explicit completion, without a fourth host outcome.

ASYNC-04.argument: Declared task/enrollment/registration fields retain typed checked relationships and monotonic run/wait identities; replacement/restart invalidates old waits before later delivery. Enrollment ownership is noncopyable and aliases cannot authorize new consumption rights.

ASYNC-05.argument: Callbacks own only native endpoints/buffers and immutable service/submission tokens. Synchronous and concurrent completion tests queue records without calling Ama; later executor import matches live registrations rather than reused addresses.

ASYNC-06.argument: Retained completion publication and explicit readiness rechecks preserve an event at every wait transition; synchronized native wake/registration tests cover check-to-sleep and publication races without callback mutation of Ama state.

ASYNC-07.argument: Ready flags and FIFO entries are changed together, duplicate readiness coalesces and voluntary yields append at tail. Finite step/import budgets and typed-queue arbitration prevent replenishment starvation; quiescence tests prohibit idle spinning.

ASYNC-08.argument: Cancellation is a visible cooperative request with one terminal commit; early cancellation, completion-before-cancel and late-event tests prove exactly one outcome and one wake without interrupting active execution.

ASYNC-09.argument: Detachment invalidates registrations while native callback records/endpoints retain independent ownership until retirement. Tests destroy/restart tasks with outstanding callbacks and verify late tokens cannot target reused storage or unload code prematurely.

ASYNC-10.argument: Continuation copying creates no enrollment/subscription. Noncopyable enrollment/native operation owners reject implicit duplication, copied continuations require fresh enrollment and shared external operations retain their explicit subscriber/consumption policy.

ASYNC-11.argument: Technical task failure ends the complete context and detaches every wait before reporting failed; no scheduler catches it as an application phase or resumes remaining tasks. Child supervision is an explicit different-context policy.

ASYNC-12.argument: Ama scheduler and explicit yielded-host boundaries use nonyielding native event operations, retained completions and finite rounds. Race/cancellation/restart/detachment tests demonstrate no lost wakeups or obsolete delivery without retained C activations.

CABI-01.argument: Native entry signatures use typed parameter/result views and a distinct technical-status service output; application failure values remain ordinary declared results independent of technical execution success.

CABI-02.argument: Exact nominal module identity selects representation and generated view types; isolated negative C probes reject wrong native types rather than accepting universal raw-word casts.

CABI-03.argument: Value installation precedes typed native entry access; const input views and typed output views refer to the callee bound interface rather than caller-owned aliases. Byte views use explicit immutable length and no borrow may outlive the operation.

CABI-04.argument: Extended-alignment native payload and stable-address tests validate typed storage; generated declarations/toolchain checks reject mismatches. Opaque resources and bounded views do not authorize private metadata casts or arbitrary relocation.

CABI-05.argument: Generated declared fields own the Ama graph and runtime fixups; opaque native payloads only own native resources. Typed-view checks enforce supported access, while isolated child-host resources follow the separately checked embedding contract, not hidden parent Ama references.

CABI-06.argument: Standalone first-include headers, untouched scaffolds, machine-readable tooling configuration and composed include-order probes validate the usable authoring interface. Unsupported backend settings and incompatible declarations fail checked native builds.

CALL-01.argument: The target resolves declared instance storage, never an executable path singleton. Binding modes, arity and input-before-output ordering are validated for the complete operation before runtime.

CALL-02.argument: Inputs/results use exact ordinary transfer semantics and entry defaults; repeated calls execute independently. Owned result transfer clones complete value state without continuation positions, while references only transfer identity.

CALL-03.argument: Read mode skips preparation/body execution and preserves initial or retained results, requiring output-phase actions. Each nested selector retains its own independently validated mode.

CALL-04.argument: Target admission has an explicit refusal provenance flag, distinct from numeric status alone. Invalid identity/availability refuses before reset or output actions; complete selected trees retain parent protection until exit.

CALL-05.argument: Only target/list documented pre-entry refusal chooses the local alternative. Constructor and decoder failures remain technical; selected-link refusal abandons pending chain actions after cleanup and cannot fall through to an ancestor handler.

CALL-06.argument: Independent input/output counters consume explicit empty positional markers without invented receivers, retain omitted-input defaults and reject excess positions, mixed styles, resume inputs and empty retained transfers.

CALL-07.argument: Exact input literal boundaries preserve raw payload bytes; destination capability chooses one fresh constructor per entry. Generated failure tests prove no body, refusal handler or result publication follows invalid construction.

CALL-08.argument: Inputs are selected in written order before reset, then installed once in declaration order before results. Outputs resolve and commit sequentially using current indices; earlier field commits survive later technical failure.

CALL-09.argument: Selected result trees retain real owned/reference instance identities, use caller operands and execute complete subtrees depth-first. Fixed caller frames protect unfinished paths; yield clears only current return links and refusal abandons the unfinished chain.

COMP-01.argument: Structural parsing precedes typed receiver inference and selector binding; missing names cannot select an alternative grammar.

COMP-02.argument: Source AST, semantic nodes, validated control/storage IR and C emission remain distinct owned representations.

COMP-03.argument: Loading reachability, eager construction, constant initialization and clone relations are separate finite analyses; benign loading cycles terminate.

COMP-04.argument: Original byte spans and source/type diagnostics survive errors; publication preserves source ownership and refuses unusable partial artifacts.

COMP-05.argument: Exact source/settings dependency comparison, checked output ownership and real Unicode clean/reused product byte comparisons preserve deterministic source/metadata. Verified executable observations cover transitive Ama/header/native/ABI/settings changes and refreshed original-source diagnostics; arbitrary external binary reproducibility is not inferred.

CONST-01.argument: Semantic checks forbid reference constants and noncopyable constant types. Shared values expose only copy-source paths; native constant-capable types additionally promise absence of hidden mutable handles, external resources and external constructor effects.

CONST-02.argument: The planner orders individual declarations by preceding declarations and actual fresh-construction value reads, rejects cycles/forward reads and deterministically chooses ready nodes. Runtime failures clean partial prefixes before root publication and shutdown reverses successful order.

CONST-03.argument: Path-plus-retained bindings select the static shared interface, independently of executable instances; tests use an alarm constructor to make accidental namespace instantiation observable.

CONST-04.argument: Named constants are ordinary nominal typed values. Their payload interpretation remains the native/library contract; shared-namespace tests exercise named finite values without language numbering or namespace execution.

CONST-05.argument: Qualified constant sources resolve the exact namespace and final declared member with preserved storage form, reject missing/mistyped/forward values and copy directly into destination storage without an implicit instance.

CONT-01.argument: Yield returns only the immediate invocation, publishes outputs and retains the instance own next label; the current caller link is retired so a later resumer supplies a new link.

CONT-02.argument: Saved labels plus explicit cursor/local control cells support suspension inside loops/branches without retained C activations. Completion clears position and absence of position refuses resume instead of entry fallback.

CONT-03.argument: Resume input lines are rejected statically, while runtime resume skips interface reset and preserves suspended parameters/results. Output binding and selected-result actions remain ordinary independently validated operations.

CONT-04.argument: Explicit continuation mode copies saved positions throughout owned state and maps cursor/local/origin identities after destination lists exist. Removed or obsolete memberships remain dead; ordinary copies discard these controls.

CONT-05.argument: Full ownership-tree availability is validated before copying, including busy descendants beneath available roots; external references are excluded. Failure-prefix tests retain source/old destination and never duplicate active return links.

CONT-06.argument: Native declarations reject Ama yield, failed execution cannot resume, and yielded state differs from an outstanding waiting invocation. Explicit host disposal cleans yielded owned state without executing remaining body statements.

COPY-01.argument: Clone work creates independent owned descendants, maps only internal references and invokes native value clone hooks. Reference-only lists preserve target identities; immutable native backing sharing remains governed by the native value contract.

COPY-02.argument: Every preparation allocation and native-constructor failure preserves the old destination; destructive commit failures clean old/prepared resources exactly once and terminally dispose failed contexts without rollback.

COPY-03.argument: Ordinary clone mode clears saved positions throughout owned descendants, while explicit continuation mode preserves them. Runtime-identical ordinary assignment is checked before cloning and preserves its original position.

COPY-04.argument: A single boundary includes the source root, all owned fields and list children. Complete identity mapping redirects root/ancestor/forward/cyclic internal handles; external targets and independently copied boundaries remain unchanged.

COPY-05.argument: All destination identities exist before reference fixups and publication; root replacement maps back to the preserved destination identity. Failure-prefix tests verify no leaked prepared state or rewritten source/external handles.

COPY-06.argument: Static capability checks apply even to identical spelling. Runtime identity permits only ordinary exact self no-op; continuation self-copy and ancestor/descendant overlap reject before hooks or mutation.

COPY-07.argument: The full source ownership tree is admitted and protected before clone hooks, including waiting owned descendants; reentry tests prove the protection remains effective. External reference targets are outside that traversal.

CORE-01.argument: The implementation has one current grammar, typed pipeline and runtime rather than version-specific alternate language mechanisms.

CORE-02.argument: Domain operations compose ordinary module/type/native contracts; closed grammar and capability tables do not add library-defined syntax.

CORE-03.argument: The canonical specification and explicit ambiguity workflow govern changes; source/type validation does not use fallback interpretations.

CORE-04.argument: Typed native declarations and generated uses are checked while native correctness, resource and toolchain assumptions remain explicit.

CORE-05.argument: Storage/call/control parsing and the closed six native protocols remain fixed independently of module spellings and native helper names.

DEBUG-01.argument: Immutable source tables and current operation/return-link selectors map checked execution back to original module/file/line/column, including selected operations rather than hashes alone.

DEBUG-02.argument: Reporting walks intact instance-owned caller links before terminal release, with initialization context and allocation-free fallback. Compiled nested native failures verify complete original-source traces before disposal.

DEBUG-03.argument: Yield retires old callers and a later resumer supplies the active trace; compiled tests reject historical original-caller entries and continuation copies never inherit their source caller chain.

DEBUG-04.argument: Native hooks return normal explicit status before runtime reporting and lifecycle cleanup; internal C recursion is not fabricated as Ama calls and no longjmp skips resource cleanup.

DEP-01.argument: Typed declarations/constant sources discover the exact root-family-qualified transitive closure without wildcard or implicit parent imports.

DEP-02.argument: The complete catalog rejects duplicates/aliases, distinguishes loading records and reports missing/draft/invalid request chains.

DEP-03.argument: Exact closure snapshots and consumer dirty fixed points include Ama/native/configuration dependencies; independent graph oracles, actual Make consumer tracking and real verified product changes test invalidation without stale output reuse or overwriting authored inputs.

EMBED-01.argument: A validated explicit export/schema model drives static/shared packages, independent public headers and ABI/build metadata. Real separate consumers link both artifact kinds without importing private runtime declarations or an implicit main/root.

EMBED-02.argument: Context creation initializes constants without root/body execution; explicit exported-root creation publishes only completed identities. Separate create/entry resets, yielded disposal and failed construction follow checked context lifecycle and reverse root order.

EMBED-03.argument: One exact executor lease spans admission, interface installation, dispatch and unpublished output construction. Invalid handles/modes/shapes reject without altering healthy state; accepted decoder/execution/transport failure terminally fails only its context.

EMBED-04.argument: Explicit recursive transport schemas reject unsupported reference-bearing shapes and build independent typed inputs/owned wire snapshots. Empty/live/released output ownership, partial allocation cleanup and retained reads are tested through real compiled native modules.

EMBED-05.argument: Application failure remains ordinary technically successful data; technical failure reports owned diagnostics and leaves only cleanup/diagnostic access. Explicit child supervision translates a returned child failure by declared policy without resuming the failed child or lending unloadable message bytes.

EMBED-06.argument: Two real static/shared components with identical Ama/native basenames link and run independently with both public headers. Checked ABI/bootstrap identities, nonwrapping host records and exact code pins prevent stale access, accidental interposition and supported unload before resource retirement.

EMBED-07.argument: A native parent owns a fresh isolated child through its checked public API, with exactly-once partial/yielded cleanup and no parent references hidden in child-control resources. Missing clone protocol rejects both ordinary and continuation copies statically.

EMBED-08.argument: Nested child entry/yield/failure returns normally through C before any outer suspension; retained child phase drives explicit later resume without new inputs. Real supervision probes reject active ancestor/same-context reentry and preserve independent caller/control boundaries.

ERROR-01.argument: Failure module condition and owned public description form one ordinary value; false/true transitions clear stale descriptions, copying retains owned text and allocation failure stays technical. Result names never infer compiler capabilities.

ERROR-02.argument: Technical failure reports cause/current execution before terminal context cleanup; prior committed transfers/effects remain. Refusal alternatives cannot catch constructor, copy, decoder or native body failure.

ERROR-03.argument: The common code/message/length C status represents zero success and bounded optional UTF-8 without terminator assumptions. Checked malformed transports and code classification never inspect translated message wording.

ERROR-04.argument: Native status messages are borrowed immutable program-lifetime bytes; streaming needs no runtime allocation. Component pins and boundary-owned reports preserve creator-code/message lifetime rather than lending destroyed child buffers.

ERROR-05.argument: A reserved invalid-index code is classified separately from technical conversion failure; failed outputs are never consumed and only documented indexed/preflight refusal reaches the operation own alternative.

ERROR-06.argument: Immediate caller service metadata saves explicit refusal before handler dispatch and retains it across successful calls; copied ordinary/continuation instances start a fresh refusal context, and readers return snapshots as successful ordinary data.

FLOW-01.argument: Structural branch polarity selects positive, negative or both bodies after one native truth conversion; empty-body syntax and saved body positions do not introduce reevaluation or lookup-dependent parsing.

FLOW-02.argument: Fixed lexical condition/body/exit labels implement repeat, break and early return. Syntactically empty bodies still select and convert once for either boolean value, then exit without repeating.

FLOW-03.argument: Only the operand type own explicit native truth/index capability is accepted with checked C signatures; no implicit integer truth or inherited child capability is introduced. Conversion errors remain technical.

FLOW-04.argument: The entire written linear header repeats from its lexical root on each backedge and releases all header protection before the body. Nested boundaries, refusal exits, indexed terminals and suspended bodies have distinct compiled tests.

FLOW-05.argument: Each candidate advances the live boundary before eligibility/body execution; exact insertion/removal corrections define future work. Scoped reference reuse, absent-entry skipping, origin guards, nested/resumed loops and empty-body nonactivation have separate tests without snapshots or target searches.

GEN-01.argument: One dependency-correct C component assembly contains all layouts, native bodies and label-based Ama execution.

GEN-02.argument: Context-local direct goto/switch control uses explicit return metadata, with no C call per Ama module.

GEN-03.argument: Cross-transfer values occupy explicit instance/control/shared storage; conservative general layouts remain valid and optional unimplemented eliminations are unclaimed.

GEN-04.argument: Resolved module/control identity determines shared emission, while distinct owned instances keep independent mutable state and source maps.

LIB-01.argument: Public native module contracts and symbolic typed protocols supply arithmetic/condition/index operations. Fixed integer size bridging is checked without universal numeric payloads or a seventh binding; real standard-module compositions test values and lifecycles.

LIB-02.argument: Shared named values use ordinary immutable namespaces, while intrinsic list actions use direct typed methods and no selector constants. Reads execute no namespace body and copied constants remain independent ordinary values.

LIFE-01.argument: Explicit construction prefixes distinguish fresh/constructing/live/finalized payloads, create children before native payload and use the reserved final identity for self initializers without exposing incomplete storage.

LIFE-02.argument: Only the selected constructor runs on fresh payload storage; unsuccessful native construction owns its partial cleanup and is never destroyed again by runtime. Completed children unwind in reverse order with the primary error retained.

LIFE-03.argument: Deletion invalidates outside access before native destruction while owned children remain available, then destroys children in reverse order exactly once. Nonowning references do not add destruction edges.

LIFE-04.argument: Complete source/destination preflight precedes private preparation and exact reference fixup. Commit preserves final root identity and either publishes the fully prepared value or terminally disposes remaining old/new resources.

LIFE-05.argument: Failure reports active context before releasing explicit links/acquisitions and reverse-published root trees, then constants. Mixed-type/reused-slot/replaced-root tests prove order comes from successful root publication, not pool layout; failure never becomes resumable.

LIST-01.argument: Each typed list owns its checked owner/field/incarnation, order, capacity and record pool independently of module instance pools; reference entries remain nonowning even when absent targets are stored.

LIST-02.argument: Current zero-based selection checks native index conversion and bounds before lookup; call targets refuse missing/stale/busy selections before interface preparation. Foreach-reference headers and whole-list service parents are structurally distinct.

LIST-03.argument: Order entries are local record indices; live records retain target, generation and current position. Bijection/growth/reuse tests enforce O(1) exact lookup and stable payloads, with geometric checked batch growth rather than linked positional order.

LIST-04.argument: All six fixed typed interfaces are specialized to exact element identities without method instances or action constants. Ephemeral results remain protected until subtree cleanup, and full-size length uses exactly one from_size constructor without literal parsing.

LIST-05.argument: Array access and record lookup are constant time, shifts preserve remaining order and update positions. Implemented fixed lexical cursor correction adds O(K), with no length-dependent traversal setup or saved history.

LIST-06.argument: Owned deletion preflights every affected descendant and retires its identity; reference-entry deletion retires only the occurrence without acquiring/destroying its still-live target. Generated tests observe both lifetime effects.

LIST-07.argument: Ordinary positional order uses compact arrays with O(n) front removal; a separate circular queue is permitted rather than required, and no alternate linked ordinary-list representation is introduced.

LIST-08.argument: Sibling append/insert/remove/clear/swap/length operations execute sequentially with precise typed arity. Swap changes occurrence order without cloning targets; self-swap and empty clear preserve membership state.

LIST-09.argument: Owning insertion either default-constructs once or independently clones a supplied target with cleared saved positions. Explicit source binding statically requires clone capability even for empty handles; reference insertion copies full handles without target acquisition.

LIST-10.argument: One exact list token and owner protection span the complete service tree, including result actions. Preflight refusal precedes mutation/output, while allocation/native constructor/destructor failures remain technical and release staged resources correctly.

LIST-11.argument: Stored length updates with committed structure; from_size produces ordinary owned length values. Whole-list copies preserve order and ownership semantics with fresh independent membership/incarnation state, never copied busy tokens or implicit cursors.

LIST-12.argument: Compiled service tests exercise default/copy insertion, positional removal with local refusal, sibling swap/length and direct element execution; live-boundary tests independently exercise future insertion and deletion behavior from the examples.

LIST-13.argument: Implemented fixed lexical scans match full collection identity and correct every active/suspended boundary before publication. Fresh membership/incarnation generations prevent reuse aliasing; atomic reference replacement preserves boundaries, and continuation copies remap identities without inherited tokens.

LIT-01.argument: The lexer identifies declaration/input literal boundaries before comment handling; payload bytes preserve spaces, hash characters and empty contents while global TAB rejection remains separate.

LIT-02.argument: Generated native byte fixtures compare explicit byte counts and raw fwrite output for UTF-8, repeated/trailing spaces and empty payloads under LF/CRLF. No terminator or wchar_t conversion participates.

LIT-03.argument: Semantic transfer assigns literal type from the declared destination and checks its literal capability; ordinary assignment/index/condition grammar has no inferred numeric-literal path.

LIT-04.argument: Native literal construction returns a technical status; generated capacity failure proves the body, refusal alternative and result publication do not run after failure. Byte/type validation remains a native contract, never arbitrary compile-time execution.

NAME-01.argument: Category/root/component framed identities drive deterministic names; checked component exports additionally qualify external linkage.

NAME-02.argument: The registry retains exact keys and rejects forced unequal-key digest collisions; fixed SHA-256 framing vectors include Unicode.

NAME-03.argument: Original byte paths/lines and operation locations survive code generation, C escaping and actual compiler diagnostics.

NAME-04.argument: Namespace construction rejects every cross-section and suffix pair for the same base name. Inference preserves source-order duplicates; scoped foreach identities remain separate only for disjoint bodies.

NAME-05.argument: Native module-prefix identities include root kind and qualify authored types/hooks consistently in standalone headers and assembly. Equal local basenames compose without context leaks; C macro/global discipline remains an explicit author obligation.

NAME-06.argument: Explicit declarations are collected for lookup while inferred fields retain introducing source positions. Lexical local intervals implement no shadowing, compatible reuse and construction-time exclusion independently of runtime branch outcomes.

PAR-01.argument: Simultaneously executed generated contexts own distinct constants, pools, diagnostics and selectors, even for colliding local triples; foreign-origin checks reject before local identity resolution.

PAR-02.argument: Explicit quiescent executor handoff publishes state through synchronization with no live native borrow; a separate thread-affine resource test refuses unsupported movement rather than treating a mutex as permission.

PAR-03.argument: Declared versioned message schemas serialize native-owned bytes and reconstruct independent typed Ama fields; malformed content is ordinary rejection while construction/allocation failure unwinds and technically fails the receiver.

PAR-04.argument: One logical sender/receiver pair atomically accepts bounded complete messages in FIFO order. Capacity releases at take; sender close drains, receiver abort releases queued data and wakes peers, and exact capacity waits preserve ownership on rejection.

PAR-05.argument: Native channel/event gates synchronize native-only state and callbacks retain no Ama access. Concurrent lifecycle/queue tests exercise the declared services; arbitrary external native dependencies still require their own affinity/thread-safety or process-isolation contract.

PAR-06.argument: A generated actor technical failure disposes only its context and closes/aborts its endpoints while a peer remains executable. Wider shutdown and application-level child failure translation remain explicit supervisor policies.

PAR-07.argument: Generated dispatch takes its admitted explicit context view; mutable pools/constants/control and diagnostics belong to that owner, not process globals or C-stack Ama activations. Child host resources are separately admitted execution domains.

PAR-08.argument: Real threaded generated execution covers private startup, reuse, foreign identities and isolated failure; channel/message/wait tests cover bounded FIFO, malformed data, close/abort/cancel and late events, supplemented by quiescent handoff/affinity probes.

PROTO-01.argument: The fixed six-symbol table supplies exact hook bindings with mandatory create/destroy and optional capabilities; exhaustive ordered capability subsets and module-qualified namespace tests forbid cross-binding equal basenames.

PROTO-02.argument: The compiler consumes binding records directly and checks mandatory/duplicate/unknown capabilities without parsing arbitrary C. Typed signature probes let the target C compiler reject incompatible hooks.

PROTO-03.argument: Conversion signatures use const payload and typed output; the exact standard integer from_size bridge constructs every supported size once over fresh storage and round-trips limb boundaries without decimal or default construction.

PROTO-04.argument: Condition/index hooks inspect the current typed payload with read-only inputs; repeated condition tests and source selection use those hooks rather than cached results, hidden body execution or universal integer truth.

PROTO-05.argument: Negative/host-overflow index results remain distinguishable from unrelated technical helper failure and leave outputs unconsumed. List bounds are checked separately using zero-based positions before mutation.

PROTO-06.argument: Explicit clone capability constructs independent payloads; immutable counted backing tests cover both destruction orders, independent replacement, rollback and reduced count exhaustion. Mutable resources and hidden Ama handles are excluded by the native author contract.

PROTO-07.argument: Capability removal computes the greatest fixed point over all owned scalar/list type edges, excluding references/constants. Exhaustive small-graph tests compare against reachability of noncopyable native seeds rather than current list contents.

PROTO-08.argument: Default, literal, clone and size-bridge paths select one fresh payload constructor after owned fields; failure leaves payload nonlive and runtime cleans only completed children. Destruction invokes native hooks without running module bodies.

PROTO-09.argument: All hooks share explicit technical status; native entry exposes the same status separately from Ama results. Generated execution distinguishes constructor/conversion/body errors from application failure values and acquisition refusal.

PROTO-10.argument: Cleanup continues after destructor errors, retains the primary status and invalidates destroyed state exactly once. Failure during destructive replacement terminally cleans old and prepared resources without restoring a partly destroyed destination.

PROTO-11.argument: The line parser enforces UTF-8 records, exact one-space separation, fixed symbols, valid native identifiers and physical diagnostics. Exhaustive subsets, truncations, malformed records and allocation failures never publish partial success.

REF-01.argument: Self sources retain the containing module identity in creation and execution; supplied caller self differs from callee defaults. Semantic checks reject reference-to-reference and mismatched destination identities.

REF-02.argument: Pool validation checks type, slot, nonzero generation and liveness; host context wrappers additionally validate context identity, while handles do not own or retain targets.

REF-03.argument: Assignments resolve the destination before the source and transfer the exact checked storage form; reference assignment changes only the stored handle. Invalid standalone selection remains technical failure without a refusal branch.

REF-04.argument: Retirement invalidates liveness before cleanup, checked access rejects empty/stale/wrong-type identities and preflight protects ownership before destruction. Nonowning cycles do not enter ownership traversal.

REF-05.argument: Reduced-generation pool tests reach exhaustion explicitly and compare bounded operation schedules with identity/occupancy invariants; exhausted slots permanently retire rather than wrap.

REF-06.argument: Entire-block and sparse-block reclamation tests retain issued identity history and reject stale handles after fresh allocations; directory growth never renumbers live slots.

REF-07.argument: Self formation works while the containing instance is running without acquiring it. Copy maps preserve empty/stale/external handle identities; later selected-target access performs independent admission checks.

REF-08.argument: Whole-tree preflight checks all owned descendants before native hooks/destruction, borrows only authorized protection and restores partial prefixes on failure; references never enlarge the affected boundary.

RT-01.argument: Every context owns its mutable type pools/constants and creates no implicit pool objects; constants-only namespaces stay pool-free.

RT-02.argument: Live instance payloads remain in stable blocks with fixed lexical control cells; general layouts preserve all metadata observations.

RT-03.argument: Constructing, busy, yielded and acquired states enforce checked access independently of payload address stability.

RT-04.argument: Busy checks select an actual instance: distinct same-type instances execute while a busy alias refuses.

RT-05.argument: Generated execution selects existing stable instance fields without a working-state save/restore mirror.

RT-06.argument: Nested calls prepare inputs separately, attach explicit caller/selector state and transfer by labels without payload relocation.

RT-07.argument: Result/action processing retains target acquisition and independent output continuations until scoped release.
